evidence: backend/servers/api-server/src/services/actions/delay.rs:54-61 `DelayConfig::to_duration()` computes `Duration::from_secs(self.duration * 60)` (Minutes), `* 3600` (Hours) and `* 86400` (Days) on `self.duration: u64` (delay.rs:44), which is deserialized directly from user-supplied workflow action config JSON via `parse_config` (delay.rs:77-80) -> `serde_json::from_value`. The multiplication is UNCHECKED and is evaluated BEFORE any bound is applied.

The 7-day cap is enforced only AFTER the multiply: `execute()` calls `to_duration()` at delay.rs:100 and then checks `if duration.as_secs() > MAX_DELAY_SECONDS` at delay.rs:103-108. Because the cap runs on the already-computed (possibly wrapped) value, it cannot catch an overflow: a large `duration` with unit=Days overflows `u64` in the `* 86400` step. In debug / `cargo test` builds (overflow-checks default ON) this PANICS with 'attempt to multiply with overflow', crashing the action-executor task — reachable from user-controlled workflow config and exercised by any test that constructs an overflowing DelayConfig. backend/Cargo.toml `[profile.release]` (lines 180-183) does NOT set `overflow-checks`, so in production release the multiply WRAPS instead: a huge configured value silently wraps to a small number that slips under MAX_DELAY_SECONDS, so the documented 7-day cap is bypassable and the workflow delays for an arbitrary wrong (shorter) duration with no error.

FIX: validate `self.duration` against the per-unit maximum BEFORE converting (or use `u64::checked_mul` and map `None` -> `ActionError::ConfigurationError`), i.e. reject/clamp at parse time rather than multiplying first and range-checking the product. Add a regression test with `duration=u64::MAX, unit=Days` asserting a clean ConfigurationError (not a panic, not a wrapped sub-cap Duration). Backend-only, statically landable.

backend/servers/api-server/src/services/auth.rs:48-66 `AuthService::new()` reads Argon2id cost parameters from env (`PPT_ARGON2_M_COST_KIB`, `PPT_ARGON2_T_COST`, `PPT_ARGON2_P_COST`) with safe numeric fallbacks (m=65536, t=3, p=1), then builds `Params::new(m_cost, t_cost, p_cost, None).expect("argon2 params hard-coded above the library minimum, cannot fail")` (auth.rs:61-62). The `.expect()` justification is STALE/incorrect: the params are env-DERIVED, not hard-coded, so 'cannot fail' no longer holds.

Two concrete gaps. (a) Fail-not-soft: an operator value below the argon2 crate minimum (e.g. `PPT_ARGON2_M_COST_KIB` below `8*p_cost`, or a zero cost) makes `Params::new` return Err, and `.expect()` PANICS at AuthService construction -> process aborts at boot with a non-actionable message, unlike the fail-fast-with-guidance pattern used for JWT_SECRET (main.rs ~539-547) and the operator-actionable panics in totp.rs. (b) Silent weakening: a value that is low-but-still-valid (above the library floor yet below the OWASP/P1-08 floor the doc comment at auth.rs:42-47 promises) is accepted with NO warning, so a misconfigured deploy hashes passwords weaker than the code claims to guarantee — defeating the documented 'tune above the OWASP minimum' hardening with zero signal.

FIX: clamp each env override up to the documented P1-08 floor (m>=19456 KiB, t>=2, p>=1) via `.max(FLOOR)` before `Params::new`, and replace the `.expect()` with a `match` that logs the effective params (so weakening is visible) and, on a genuine `Params::new` error, emits an operator-actionable message. Update the stale 'hard-coded ... cannot fail' comment. Backend-only, statically landable.
